beads.title: Race the upstream DNS TCP hop against a slow or failed UDP hop, as Go's forwarder does
beads.description: The MagicDNS forwarder falls back to TCP only when an upstream answer is truncated. Go also falls back when the UDP hop is slow or fails. At commit e2ed432399c9b0fda7aa14e9eb27784d2d893c55, net/dns/resolver/forwarder.go send (line 627) does not ask over UDP and then decide. It hands two closures to race.New(timeout, firstUDP, thenTCP) (forwarder.go:744). util/race/race.go Race.Start (race.go:58) runs firstUDP at once, and runs thenTCP when the timeout elapses (race.go:70) or when firstUDP returns an error (race.go:102 closes startFallback), whichever comes first. The first non-error answer wins. Three behaviours follow. (1) SLOW OR FAILED UDP FALLS BACK TO TCP. For a UDP client the timeout is udpRaceTimeout, 2 seconds (forwarder.go:108, :738). For a TCP client it is 0 (:740), so TCP starts alongside UDP. A resolver whose UDP path drops or stalls but whose TCP path answers still resolves, in about two seconds. (2) A TRUNCATED ANSWER IS RETRIED OVER TCP TO THE SAME RESOLVER. firstUDP maps it to truncatedResponseError (:722). (3) A UDP CLIENT'S TRUNCATED ANSWER IS NOT RETRIED. firstUDP returns it as it came when isUDPQuery (:707), because the client can retry over TCP itself. skipTCP (:677, the dns-forwarder-disable-tcp-retries knob) gates all three: under it, thenTCP waits on the context and never dials. This repository has (2) only, and runs it sequentially. #440 ported it into ts_runtime/src/magic_dns.rs. ask_with_tcp_retry (magic_dns.rs:1248) awaits the UDP hop to completion, bounded only by UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT, 5 seconds (:93). A UDP hop that errors or times out returns None before TCP is considered, so the walk moves to the next resolver or ends in SERVFAIL; that is the missing (1). forward_query (:1158) passes the client transport to forward_walk but not to ask_upstream, so a truncated answer is re-asked over TCP for a UDP client as well; that inverts (3) and opens a TCP connection to the resolver that a Go node on the same tailnet does not. The doc comment on ask_upstream (:1203) says Go's forwarder 'does exactly this'; correct it with the port. Keep everything #440 got right. The retry goes to the same resolver, never the next one. A failed TCP retry relays the truncated UDP answer. An answer that fit is never retried. The forged-TC check stays in place. Both hops ride the overlay netstack Channel and never a host socket, which is an anti-leak invariant here. TcpRetry::Disabled must gate the new race arm too. The decision to make: port all three behaviours, or port (1) and record (3) as a deliberate divergence with its reason. Test the refusals as well as the fallback. A resolver that never answers UDP but answers TCP must resolve within the race timeout, and must not wait out UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT. With the attribute set, no TCP connection may be opened on any arm. A UDP client's truncated answer must come back without a TCP hop if (3) is ported. Upstream's TestForwarderNetstackUpstream (forwarder_test.go) bounds elapsed time by udpRaceTimeout because this fallback can hide a broken UDP path behind the right bytes arriving two seconds late; copy that shape. Resolver- and client-observable, not peer-observable. See PORTING.md section B.
